statements.subject: Language and Literacy
statements.text: Attention and listening skills through: (a) listening to a wide range of stories, poems, songs and music (b) following instructions (c) identifying environmental sounds (d) repeating familiar phrases/sound sequences (e) recalling sequence and detail.

statements.subject: Language and Literacy
statements.text: Phonological awareness through: (a) responding to a steady beat (b) identifying words in phrases and sentences (c) identifying syllables (d) identifying and generating rhymes (e) identifying and manipulating phonemes.

statements.subject: Language and Literacy
statements.text: Social use of language through: (a) observing modelled behaviours (b) understanding non-verbal signals (c) talking with adults and other pupils (d) initiating and joining in conversations in pairs or groups (e) working in different groupings (f) adopting or assuming a role relevant to context.

statements.subject: Language and Literacy
statements.text: Language and thinking through: (a) talking about experiences, pictures and stories (b) talking about their work, play and things they have made (c) naming (d) recalling (e) sequencing (f) predicting (g) asking and answering questions (h) describing (i) explaining (j) sharing their thoughts, feelings and ideas with different audiences (k) taking part/contributing to group oral language activities.

statements.subject: Language and Literacy

statements.subject: Physical Development and Movement
statements.text: Athletics: Pupils should be provided with opportunities for activities and physical challenges enabling them to learn, understand and develop the core skills of running, jumping and throwing in a co-operative context.

statements.subject: Physical Development and Movement
statements.text: Dance: Pupils should be given opportunities to respond to a variety of stimuli and the use of body movements to communicate ideas and express feelings.

statements.subject: Physical Development and Movement
statements.text: Games: Pupils should be taught to develop games skills through a range of activities and using a variety of equipment.

statements.subject: Physical Development and Movement
statements.text: Gymnastics: Pupils should be taught to explore, create, practice and improve body management skills.
